title: The site plan draws the parcel's own outline: the results document's lot outline comes from the measured tax-map polygon (translated to local feet, its area equal to the measured outline area), never a rectangle sized to the recorded lot area; with no outline, no outline is drawn and the geometry says why
objective: Correct the program's drawing geometry (the owner's review, row R896): `services/api/app/scenario/three_answers/geometry.py` draws an axis-aligned rectangle whose area equals the RECORDED lot area (10,075 sq ft on the benchmark lot) and the site plan labels it as the tax-map outline (10,387.99 sq ft). The lot outline must come from the measured tax-map polygon the results path already reads for the area comparison, translated to local feet with the transform stated; where there is no outline, nothing is drawn and the reason is given. No legal figure changes.
business_reason: The owner's reviewer found that the site plan and the measurement explanation disagree; the presentation contract forbids a pleasant rectangle in place of the actual lot and stretching the outline to the recorded area (rows R841, R846).
inputs: the outline gathered in result_way_bridge.py and threaded by result_way_engine_bridge.py (as wave 19 threaded the lot areas)
services/api/app/drawings/kit/ (the site plan and its labels)
the committed benchmark document and its drawing and CAD snapshots
outputs: the outline threaded into the geometry block
the benchmark document and its snapshots regenerated
tests that the drawn outline's area equals the measured outline area and that no outline means no drawing

acceptance_scenarios.case: The benchmark lot draws its own outline
acceptance_scenarios.input: the recorded journey for 215-16 Northern Boulevard
acceptance_scenarios.expected: geometry.lot_outline is the measured tax-map polygon in local feet; its area equals the measured outline area (10,387.99 sq ft, within 0.5 sq ft); it is not a rectangle sized to 10,075 sq ft; the transform from the measured coordinates is stated in the measurement record.

acceptance_scenarios.input: the live route with no outline (the spatial provider off)
acceptance_scenarios.expected: no lot outline is drawn and the geometry gives the reason (the lot's outline is not available); no rectangle is drawn from the recorded area.
the dimension labels are the measured polygon's edge lengths; the measurement note names the tax-map outline and the transform; no label claims a basis the drawing does not use.
only the geometry block changes; no legal figure, no withheld value, no reason outside geometry; the CAD snapshot follows the same outline.

acceptance_scenarios.input: the benchmark outline's area by the shoelace formula in the test, and the recorded measurement
acceptance_scenarios.expected: the two agree within 0.5 sq ft; the expected figure is parsed from the recorded measurement, never retyped from a program run.

acceptance_scenarios.case: Layers that scale the lot shape
acceptance_scenarios.expected: a layer that would scale the lot shape into a footprint or an envelope is not drawn unless a placement is worked (ruling W5 of wave 19); where it was drawn before, it is now withheld with its reason, and the change is listed.

risks: The drawing kit's dimension labels assume rectangle edges: a polygon may need its label placement checked (contract section 6).
Other committed valid documents with geometry may change; each change is listed.
path_notes:
ONE builder (geospatial-engineer). The register is resynced inside this task if a calculation entry's code identity changes. A builder who finds the outline is not available on a path STOPS and reports which paths have it.

THE ORCHESTRATOR'S RULINGS FOR WAVE 20 (they govern; later over earlier). V1: three tasks on ONE branch, reviewed at ONE head, merged as ONE pull request: M5-T148 (shared presentation), M5-T149 (the website slice, after M5-T148) and M5-T150 (the parcel's own outline; server only, beside M5-T148). Order: M5-T148 parts A and B and M5-T150 side by side (three builders, disjoint files); integrate; then M5-T149 parts A, B and C side by side (three builders); then the orchestrator builds the website, runs the browser tests (stopping the owner's preview for the run and restarting it), takes the pictures and starts the reviews. V2: the website types no number, label, condition or reason; the presentation adapters only format numbers and group what the document says; they decide no law and recalculate nothing (D-090 R855). V3: the screen's statuses stay as the owner decided (row R641: 'Preliminary zoning results'; settled, conditional, not known); the owner's question C2 (the PDF's six labels on the screen) is open; 'Verified' is never shown. V4: the font token equals the application's existing font stack (`apps/web/src/app/layout.tsx`); no font changes in this wave. V5: a floor schedule whose placement and site fit are not established is never called 'achieved' (row R895): it is the 'scheduled area', with 'site fit not verified' beside it, before any caveat; the option comparison uses ONE wording per situation (row R894). V6: builders never start Next, Playwright or any server, and never touch ports 3000, 3001 or 8000 (the owner's preview); the orchestrator runs the browser tests. V7: a builder who finds that a file outside its part must change STOPS and reports. V8: nothing is called feasible, compliant, verified, optimal or preferred; a withheld value shows no number anywhere. V9: the estimate on the benchmark lot is 17.27 to 21.59 apartments (from the document); the planning draft's '22.20' was wrong.
